title: Distinguish module exports from supported package entry points
applies_when: A JavaScript or TypeScript helper is declared export function, or an implementation accepts a broad argument union, and a candidate assumes package users have that same API; especially native-binding packages with explicit exports or abstract public overloads.
lesson: Trace the published entry's re-exports and the package export map before building a native runtime to reproduce an isolated helper defect. A module-level export alone does not establish a supported package API. In LanceDB ca275b6, arrow.ts declares several incorrectly copied type guards, but index.ts re-exports only selected Arrow helpers and the package export map does not expose the Arrow submodule. Check public overloads too: Table.update accepts wrapped values/valuesSql with inline where, or legacy bare SQL updates with a second options argument. LocalTable's implementation union does not make the mixed wrapped-values-plus-second-options call a supported typed API. Check documented JavaScript behavior and actual callers separately. Defer a user-facing bugfix claim if supported reachability is still unproved.
avoid_when: Do not reject genuinely public helpers merely because no internal caller exists. Export maps do not cover every alias, generated bundle, older release or consumer environment. Type rejection does not prove a JavaScript call is unsupported, harmless or unreachable; inspect documented JS use before choosing a type-only or runtime repair. A partially unresolved TypeScript program is not a passing package type check. These pinned source mechanisms are not native database qualification, proof of no possible use or a reason to silently ignore a supported data-integrity failure.

evidence.note: Several guard declarations use Utf8, and isUnion uses Struct. This supports a local source discrepancy only; it does not establish supported API exposure or native behavior.
The package entry selectively re-exports makeArrowTable, makeJsonField, MakeArrowTableOptions, Data and VectorColumnOptions, not the affected guards.
The exports map exposes the main entry and three embedding entries, not an Arrow subpath. Source manifest evidence, not an installed-package resolution test.

The three public abstract update overloads separate inline values/valuesSql options from the two-argument legacy SQL form. The wider concrete implementation at lines1123-1180 ignores second options in wrapped branches, but that alone does not prove a supported public-call regression.
